title: Retain Forest hyperedge source cardinality in the canonical compiler receipt
finding: GPU-43 made retained ForestHyperedge evidence an explicit fail-closed projection boundary, but an explicitly selected unrelated binary relation could still compile with a compact receipt that reported binary Forest edges and verified bindings without reporting that higher-arity Forest evidence existed in the bound source.

implementation.summary: Extend the existing CompiledRelationBlocks receipt with forest_hyperedge_count, validate it as an exact non-negative integer alongside the existing receipt counts, include it in canonical serialization/digest material, and populate it from len(forest.hyperedges). The count remains a source cardinality even when an unrelated explicitly selected binary relation is the only materialized block; no hyperedge is flattened or reinterpreted.

focused_contracts: receipts for Forests without retained hyperedges report forest_hyperedge_count == 0
an explicitly selected unrelated binary relation over a Forest with retained higher-arity evidence reports the full source hyperedge count
forest_hyperedge_count is part of CompiledRelationBlocks.to_dict() and therefore its canonical digest material
existing GPU-43 fail-closed behavior for discover-all and conflicting relation selection remains unchanged
